**Some statements now cite their source in the text.** Where a sentence rests on a specific study or document, the source is now named in the form “(see Author Year)” or “(see ID Year)”, for example in [Task 3.6: Mitigate Automation Complacency and Skills Degradation](#task-3.6:-mitigate-automation-complacency-and-skills-degradation), [Implementation 4.5.1: Define Engineering Time-Constant Thresholds](#implementation-4.5.1:-define-engineering-time-constant-thresholds), [Implementation 4.6.1: Design Rationale Displays that Give Personnel Something to Check](#implementation-4.6.1:-design-rationale-displays-that-give-personnel-something-to-check), [Implementation 6.1.2: Require SIBOM for Mission-Critical Applications](#implementation-6.1.2:-require-sibom-for-mission-critical-applications) and [Implementation 6.1.5: Operational SI Hazard Reachability Disclosures](#implementation-6.1.5:-operational-si-hazard-reachability-disclosures).

**Corrections.** The example in [Implementation 2.1.2: Develop Process-Informed Guardrails](#implementation-2.1.2:-develop-process-informed-guardrails) had the operating conditions reversed; guardrails now allow more headroom during quieter periods and tighter control during rapid change or heightened activity. Several pointers to where an adjacent concern is handled now point to a more specific item, most notably from [Task 3.9: Assess and Document Organizational Readiness for Each SI-Enabled Capability](#task-3.9:-assess-and-document-organizational-readiness-for-each-si-enabled-capability) and [Practice 5: Implement Identity and Access Management (IdAM) for SI Agents, Systems, and Tools](#practice-5:-implement-identity-and-access-management-\(idam\)-for-si-agents,-systems,-and-tools) to [Task 13.2: Withdraw All Authority and Confirm the Result](#task-13.2:-withdraw-all-authority-and-confirm-the-result) rather than [Task 7.6: Establish Processes for Internal SI Component Deprecation and Decommissioning](#task-7.6:-establish-processes-for-internal-si-component-deprecation-and-decommissioning), and from [Practice 13: Establish Procedures for Retiring SI Systems and Withdrawing Their Authority](#practice-13:-establish-procedures-for-retiring-si-systems-and-withdrawing-their-authority) to [Implementation 2.3.4: Recurrent Risk Evaluations](#implementation-2.3.4:-recurrent-risk-evaluations) and [Implementation 3.9.2: Define Decision Authority and Reassessment Triggers](#implementation-3.9.2:-define-decision-authority-and-reassessment-triggers) rather than [Practice 2: Define SI Robustness, Resilience, and Quality of Service Expectations](#practice-2:-define-si-robustness,-resilience,-and-quality-of-service-expectations).

**Other clarifications.** Table 2 relates the Reliable, Robust and Resilient characteristics to the terms of a typical service-level agreement, and revises the Bias Managed and Fair entries. [Implementation 2.2.2: Deploy “Watchdog” Controllers](#implementation-2.2.2:-deploy-“watchdog”-controllers) notes that a watchdog may itself be part of the attack surface. The References field description notes that citation descriptions are meant to help locate successors to revised or superseded documents. Search Keywords were added in [Practices 2: Define SI Robustness, Resilience, and Quality of Service Expectations](#practice-2:-define-si-robustness,-resilience,-and-quality-of-service-expectations), [Practice 3: Define Risks, Policies, and Oversight for Automated, Agentic, and SI Behavior](#practice-3:-define-risks,-policies,-and-oversight-for-automated,-agentic,-and-si-behavior), [Practice 4: Define Procedures for Emergency Avoidance Override, Recovery, and Situational Awareness](#practice-4:-define-procedures-for-emergency-avoidance-override,-recovery,-and-situational-awareness), [Practice 5: Implement Identity and Access Management (IdAM) for SI Agents, Systems, and Tools](#practice-5:-implement-identity-and-access-management-\(idam\)-for-si-agents,-systems,-and-tools) and [Practice 8: Incorporate SI-Aware Incident Analysis and Response Procedures](#practice-8:-incorporate-si-aware-incident-analysis-and-response-procedures), and reviewer notes were added on the crosswalks, the glossary, and record retention for retired systems.

## Sep 13, 2026 {#sep-13,-2026}

This entry is organized by what changed rather than by where, because most of what follows was answered in more than one place. Feedback on the August draft was often combined with related input and addressed somewhere other than where it was raised, sometimes at a different level of the table, and sometimes through several smaller changes that only add up when read together. If you are looking for whether something you raised was acted on, you may find it more quickly by scanning the themes below than by returning to the cell you commented on.

We have indicated where changes apply substantially to only part of the document. No Practice, Task or Implementation has been removed; everything present in the August draft is still there.

**A thirteenth Practice covers retiring AI systems.** [Practice 13: Establish Procedures for Retiring SI Systems and Withdrawing Their Authority](#practice-13:-establish-procedures-for-retiring-si-systems-and-withdrawing-their-authority) treats the permanent removal of an AI capability as its own problem rather than as an extreme form of updating one: an update transfers trust from one version to the next, while retirement withdraws authority, removes a capability other things have come to rely on, and destroys operational knowledge that may exist nowhere else. [Task 13.1: Prepare for Retirement While the System Is Still Running](#task-13.1:-prepare-for-retirement-while-the-system-is-still-running) covers what has to be prepared while the system still runs, because retirement can be imposed by a withdrawn vendor or a deprecated model and can arrive after the system has stopped working. [Task 13.2: Withdraw All Authority and Confirm the Result](#task-13.2:-withdraw-all-authority-and-confirm-the-result) covers withdrawing authority completely and confirming it. [Task 13.3: Preserve What Is Needed and Hand Over What Depended on the System](#task-13.3:-preserve-what-is-needed-and-hand-over-what-depended-on-the-system) covers preserving evidence that teardown would destroy and recording what happens to everything that depended on the system. The existing treatment of internal AI artifacts, in [Task 7.6: Establish Processes for Internal SI Component Deprecation and Decommissioning](#task-7.6:-establish-processes-for-internal-si-component-deprecation-and-decommissioning), is unchanged; [Practice 13: Establish Procedures for Retiring SI Systems and Withdrawing Their Authority](#practice-13:-establish-procedures-for-retiring-si-systems-and-withdrawing-their-authority) addresses the operating capability and its authority rather than the models, datasets and pipelines themselves.

**Placeholder Implementations are now written, most heavily in [Practice 5: Implement Identity and Access Management (IdAM) for SI Agents, Systems, and Tools](#practice-5:-implement-identity-and-access-management-\(idam\)-for-si-agents,-systems,-and-tools) and [Practice 11: Maintain SI-Aware Mission Continuity and Disaster Recovery Planning](#practice-11:-maintain-si-aware-mission-continuity-and-disaster-recovery-planning).** Thirty-two Implementations that carried a single line of intent in the August draft now carry actual guidance. Nine of them are in [Practice 5: Implement Identity and Access Management (IdAM) for SI Agents, Systems, and Tools](#practice-5:-implement-identity-and-access-management-\(idam\)-for-si-agents,-systems,-and-tools), covering AI agent identity, access mapping, action-level authorization, permission scope, and logging and anomaly detection for agent activity. Nine more are in [Practice 11: Maintain SI-Aware Mission Continuity and Disaster Recovery Planning](#practice-11:-maintain-si-aware-mission-continuity-and-disaster-recovery-planning), covering process ranking, dependency mapping, manual fallback, safe operating mode, standby personnel and infrastructure, re-engagement validation, and fail-to-manual exercises. If you passed over either Practice in August because there was little to review, they are worth a second look.

**Organizational readiness is now something to assess and record before adopting an AI capability.** New [Task 3.9: Assess and Document Organizational Readiness for Each SI-Enabled Capability](#task-3.9:-assess-and-document-organizational-readiness-for-each-si-enabled-capability), with [Implementation 3.9.1: Establish Accountable Ownership](#implementation-3.9.1:-establish-accountable-ownership), [Implementation 3.9.2: Define Decision Authority and Reassessment Triggers](#implementation-3.9.2:-define-decision-authority-and-reassessment-triggers), [Implementation 3.9.3: Establish Escalation to Empowered Authority](#implementation-3.9.3:-establish-escalation-to-empowered-authority), [Implementation 3.9.4: Assess Operational Capability](#implementation-3.9.4:-assess-operational-capability), and [Implementation 3.9.5: Demonstrate Operational Enforceability](#implementation-3.9.5:-demonstrate-operational-enforceability) covering accountable ownership, decision authority and reassessment triggers, escalation to an empowered authority, operational capability, and demonstrated enforceability. Related material sits in [Task 3.6: Mitigate Automation Complacency and Skills Degradation](#task-3.6:-mitigate-automation-complacency-and-skills-degradation) on maintaining human capability and in [Implementation 9.2.1: Include Role-Specific Training on SI Failure Modes](#implementation-9.2.1:-include-role-specific-training-on-si-failure-modes) and [Implementation 9.2.2: Implement Realistic Incident Simulation Training](#implementation-9.2.2:-implement-realistic-incident-simulation-training) on role-specific training.

**Near-misses can now be reported without the reporter bearing the cost.** New [Task 8.6: Establish Non-Punitive Reporting for SI-Related Near-Misses](#task-8.6:-establish-non-punitive-reporting-for-si-related-near-misses), with [Implementation 8.6.1: Separate Benefit-Claiming from Risk-Reporting](#implementation-8.6.1:-separate-benefit-claiming-from-risk-reporting) on separating benefit-claiming from risk-reporting, [Implementation 8.6.2: Protect Reporter Identity Through an Independent Reporting Route](#implementation-8.6.2:-protect-reporter-identity-through-an-independent-reporting-route) on protecting reporter identity through an independent route, [Implementation 8.6.3: Ensure Supplier Terms Do Not Penalize Degradation Disclosure](#implementation-8.6.3:-ensure-supplier-terms-do-not-penalize-degradation-disclosure) on supplier terms that penalize disclosure, and [Implementation 8.6.4: Share De-Identified Incident Records for Collective Learning](#implementation-8.6.4:-share-de-identified-incident-records-for-collective-learning) on sharing de-identified records. [Implementation 9.2.3: Recognizing Disincentives to Reporting SI Issues](#implementation-9.2.3:-recognizing-disincentives-to-reporting-si-issues) addresses recognizing the disincentives themselves.

**External AI components are now tracked from procurement through end of life.** [Implementation 6.1.1: Add SI Disclosure to Existing Procurement Policies](#implementation-6.1.1:-add-si-disclosure-to-existing-procurement-policies) on AI disclosure in procurement policy and [Implementation 6.1.2: Require SIBOM for Mission-Critical Applications](#implementation-6.1.2:-require-sibom-for-mission-critical-applications) on requiring an AI Bill of Materials, and [Implementation 6.2.1: Register Externally Sourced SI Components in Asset Management Systems](#implementation-6.2.1:-register-externally-sourced-si-components-in-asset-management-systems), [Implementation 6.2.2: Track Vendor Updates and Third-Party Entity Changes Through Change Management Process](#implementation-6.2.2:-track-vendor-updates-and-third-party-entity-changes-through-change-management-process), and [Implementation 6.2.3: Manage End-of-Life Transitions for Externally Sourced SI Components](#implementation-6.2.3:-manage-end-of-life-transitions-for-externally-sourced-si-components) on registering externally sourced components, tracking vendor updates and third-party changes through change management, and managing end-of-life transitions.

**An AI entity’s authority can be bounded, delegated and withdrawn.** [Implementation 5.3.2: Task-Bounded and Revocable Agent Authority](#implementation-5.3.2:-task-bounded-and-revocable-agent-authority) became Task-Bounded and Revocable Agent Authority, [Implementation 5.2.2: Action-Level, Context-Aware Authorization Policies](#implementation-5.2.2:-action-level,-context-aware-authorization-policies) became Action-level, context-aware authorization policies, and new [Implementation 5.3.3: Separate Privilege via Encapsulated Downstream Agents and Tools](#implementation-5.3.3:-separate-privilege-via-encapsulated-downstream-agents-and-tools) covers separating privilege through encapsulated downstream agents and tools.

**Constraints on AI behavior are now required to be enforced independently of the AI system.** [Implementation 3.2.2: Define and Independently Enforce Deterministic Operational Constraints](#implementation-3.2.2:-define-and-independently-enforce-deterministic-operational-constraints) became “Define and independently enforce deterministic operational constraints”, and [Practice 12: Independently Verify SI-Generated Operational Logic and Artifacts Across Their Lifecycle](#practice-12:-independently-verify-si-generated-operational-logic-and-artifacts-across-their-lifecycle) became “Independently verify AI-generated operational logic and artifacts across their lifecycle”. Both titles changed to carry that point rather than imply it.

**In [Practices 1](#practice-1:-establish-requirements-for-success) to 6, each Practice and Task now states what it does not cover and where the adjacent concern is handled.** This is the combined effect of three rebuilt fields: the AI RMF mappings now say what an item contributes and what it does not; the trustworthiness entries state the limits of each contribution; and reference descriptions name the part of a source that applies and where it stops. [Practices 7](#practice-7:-manage-internal-si-supply-chain-and-data-provenance) to 12 have not yet had this work and carry markers instead; [Practice 13: Establish Procedures for Retiring SI Systems and Withdrawing Their Authority](#practice-13:-establish-procedures-for-retiring-si-systems-and-withdrawing-their-authority) was written on the new scheme from the start.

**The AI RMF mapping field was replaced rather than renamed.** “Primary AI RMF Mappings” is now “Related AI RMF subcategories”, and the change is one of meaning: listing a subcategory indicates that an item can contribute toward that outcome, not that following it satisfies the subcategory. If you commented on the previous field, the basis of that comment has changed.

**References now say which part of a source applies and why it is cited here.** Each entry opens with a label for the kind of document, and the description names the clause, section or control that bears on the item. This has been done for [Practices 1](#practice-1:-establish-requirements-for-success) to 6 and 13; [Practices 7](#practice-7:-manage-internal-si-supply-chain-and-data-provenance) to 12 retain their earlier reference lists.

**Cross-references now carry the title of what they point to.** Every internal reference in the table is a link showing the name of the target Practice, Task or Implementation, rather than an item number alone.

**Human oversight has a defined vocabulary.** The Glossary and Terminology Crosswalk now defines human oversight together with oversight mode, oversight capacity, oversight threshold and oversight authority, and these terms are used consistently through the table.

**An appendix is reserved for crosswalks to external frameworks.** [Appendix D](#appendix-d:-crosswalks) is now Crosswalks, and is a placeholder under development. The reviewer material that was [Appendix D](#appendix-d:-crosswalks) in the August draft became [Appendix E](#appendix-e:-suggested-ways-to-use-this-document-with-an-llm-based-assistant) (it is now in its own separate section at the end of the document). If you have notes referring to “[Appendix D](#appendix-d:-crosswalks)”, check which one you meant.

**The profile states that it covers high-consequence applications beyond critical infrastructure.** This was implicit in the August draft and is now stated in the title and carried through the Introduction and Scope.

**Search Keywords updated across the document.** These have been chosen to both assist readers (and their AI assistants) in locating relevant Practices and Tasks in this document, as well as to provide candidate keywords for readers to use when searching other resources.

### Cells whose text was substantially rewritten {#cells-whose-text-was-substantially-rewritten}

Thirty Practices, Tasks and Implementations that carried substantive text in the August draft have been materially rewritten, over and above the thirty-two placeholders now written out and the thirty-two cells that are new. If you commented on any of these, the text you commented on has changed.

| Location | What changed |
| :---- | :---- |
| **1** | Requirements now cover the end-to-end system, not the AI component alone; states that deciding against AI is a valid outcome |
| **1.1.2** | Expanded from a requirements matrix into named categories: task and mission scope, dependencies, and the operational system around the AI |
| **1.3.1** | Test suites now scale to consequence tier, with nominal and boundary envelope testing named |
| **1.3.4** | Evidence now pairs governance artifacts with technical artifacts |
| **1.4** | Scoped to systems that interact in natural language, and extended to ontologies, graphical conventions and multimodal output |
| **2.2** | Recast from "integrate non-AI backups" to a risk-proportionate redundancy strategy matched to consequence severity |
| **2.2.1** | Same recasting at implementation level, with a redundancy gradient tied to risk thresholds |
| **2.2.2** | Watchdogs must not themselves introduce unmanaged complexity or new attack surface |
| **2.3.3** | Substantially expanded: digital twins and hardware-in-the-loop, beyond offline data replay |
| **2.3.4** | Re-evaluation is now periodic **and** trigger-based, with distribution drift defined |
| **2.5** | Adds the worked example of a learned policy depending on out-of-specification component behavior |
| **2.5.1** | Training across the full operating range, with simulation and synthetic parameter cycling |
| **3** | Now states its relationship to [Practices 1](#practice-1:-establish-requirements-for-success), 2 and 4, and separates deterministic boundaries from human intervention |
| **3.2.1** | Intercept points may be enforced at more than one location; introduces the guarded proxy architecture |
| **3.2.5** | A reviewer must hold authority to reject and capacity to examine; presence of a reviewer is not verification |
| **3.6** | Reframed: reliance on AI is the intended result of adopting it, and practice has to be arranged rather than assumed |
| **3.8.3** | Couples the risk surface to the time-constant thresholds, since a widened surface can cross a previously satisfied threshold |
| **4** | Now points to [Practice 11: Maintain SI-Aware Mission Continuity and Disaster Recovery Planning](#practice-11:-maintain-si-aware-mission-continuity-and-disaster-recovery-planning) for sustained manual operation |
| **4.4.3** | Rewritten: reduced staffing is named as an expected benefit, and oversight capacity is drawn from the pool that benefit reduces |
| **4.5** | Oversight of any mode fails where the event outruns what the operator can be relied on to do; thresholds make this testable |
| **4.5.1** | Rebuilt around what intervention can be relied upon at minutes versus seconds, rather than a single reaction-time figure |
| **6.1.5** | Extended to contextual hazard reachability attestations and their use in alarm suppression |
| **7.4** | Separates who may act on the system from whether a specific action is permitted at execution time |
| **7.4.1** | Approvals and logging framed around reduced oversight modes and automation bias; records the evidence an approval rested on |
| **10.1.2** | Adds the inference receipt: the data elements, thresholds and configuration that produced an output |
| **11.5.2** | Simulation drills now require at least one full loss of AI infrastructure |
| **12.1** | Accountable ownership now routes to [Task 3.9: Assess and Document Organizational Readiness for Each SI-Enabled Capability](#task-3.9:-assess-and-document-organizational-readiness-for-each-si-enabled-capability) rather than being defined only here |
| **12.1.3** | Authorization roles sit within the decision authority documented at [Implementation 3.9.2: Define Decision Authority and Reassessment Triggers](#implementation-3.9.2:-define-decision-authority-and-reassessment-triggers) |
| **3.2.5, 4.1.1, 3.8.1** | Changed only by relocating a citation into the References field or adding a cross-reference; the guidance itself is unchanged |

Note: Versions “Sep 13, 2026 (a)” and “Sep 13, 2026 (b)” only differ by line/breaks, table spacing, and this note.

## Aug 3, 2026 {#aug-3,-2026}

### 1\. Document Scope & Formatting Updates {#1\.-document-scope-&-formatting-updates}

* **Markdown Availability & Parsing Guidance (*Document Structure*)**: Updated from HTML to Markdown for AI assistant pre-processing. Added explicit warnings that pre-processors may truncate table rows or appendices unless directed to parse the document in its entirety.  
* **General-Purpose AI Assistants (*Section 1.2: Scope*)**: Expanded scope to explicitly cover general-purpose AI tools (e.g., code, configuration, or procedure generators; summarizers). Added the concept of “second-order risk,” noting that engineer review of AI-generated output does not eliminate operational risk when deployed to OT/ICS environments.

### 2\. Brand New Tasks & Major Structural Additions {#2\.-brand-new-tasks-&-major-structural-additions}

* [**Task 3.8:** Scope and Map the Expanded SI Attack Surface and Risk Surface](#task-3.8:-scope-and-map-the-expanded-si-attack-surface-and-risk-surface): Added a dedicated task explicitly bifurcating exposure into adversarial threats (**AI Attack Surface**) and systemic/operational non-adversarial failure modes across all 7 SICI Trustworthiness Characteristics (**AI Risk Surface**).  
* [**Task 4.5:** Define Operational Regimes for Human-on-the-Loop and Human-Out-of-the-Loop Operation](#task-4.5:-define-operational-regimes-for-human-on-the-loop-and-human-out-of-the-loop-operation): Added controls for processes with tight time constants where real-time human intervention should not serve as a primary risk mitigation control.  
* [**Implementation 3.3.3:** Actionable Operator Decision & Escalation Pathways](#implementation-3.3.3:-actionable-operator-decision-&-escalation-pathways): Added four operational response buckets (*Trust & Execute*, *Spot-Check & Investigate*, *Escalate to Oversight*, *Immediate Emergency Override*).  
* [**Implementation 4.2.3:** Human-Centered Interfaces for SI Uncertainty and Actionable Triggers](#implementation-4.2.3:-human-centered-interfaces-for-si-uncertainty-and-actionable-triggers): Suggests requirements for HSI/HMI displays (visual confidence bands, rationale summaries); [Implementation 4.6.2: Derive Confidence and Rationale for Learned Components from Their Decision Processes](#implementation-4.6.2:-derive-confidence-and-rationale-for-learned-components-from-their-decision-processes) explicitly recommends against post-hoc attribution tools (e.g., SHAP, LIME) for primary operator rationale displays.  
* [**Implementation 6.1.5:** Operational SI Hazard Reachability Disclosures](#implementation-6.1.5:-operational-si-hazard-reachability-disclosures): Adapts VEX principles to AI by separating standard software CVE VEX from *Contextual Hazard Reachability* for probabilistic model behaviors.  
* [**Implementation 8.1.5:** Multi-Agent Cascade Reconstruction Capabilities](#implementation-8.1.5:-multi-agent-cascade-reconstruction-capabilities) **& [Implementation 8.1.6: Incident Triage Across the Dual Attack/Risk Surface](#implementation-8.1.6:-incident-triage-across-the-dual-attack/risk-surface)**: Added guidance to differentiate cyber intrusions from non-adversarial algorithmic failures.  
* [**Implementation 10.1.3:** Forensic Integrity and Privacy-Preserving Log Partitioning](#implementation-10.1.3:-forensic-integrity-and-privacy-preserving-log-partitioning): Added guidance on log partitioning to route raw unredacted text/prompts directly into appropriately isolated, secure, tamper-evident storage.  
* [**Implementation 11.2.3:** Human Factors and Cognitive Transition Protocols for Control Handoffs](#implementation-11.2.3:-human-factors-and-cognitive-transition-protocols-for-control-handoffs) **& [Implementation 11.2.4: Unplanned Shutdown and Controlled Isolation Protocols](#implementation-11.2.4:-unplanned-shutdown-and-controlled-isolation-protocols)**: Added *State-at-Handoff* displays and controlled isolation steps to reduce operator “cold start” cognitive shock during forced manual handoffs.

### 3\. Key Conceptual Revisions to Existing Controls {#3\.-key-conceptual-revisions-to-existing-controls}

* **TEVV Production Guidance (*[Implementation 1.3.1](#implementation-1.3.1:-define-tevv-scope-and-requirements-per-si-system): Define TEVV Scope and Requirements per SI System* *& [Implementation 1.3.2](#implementation-1.3.2:-categorization-of-testing-environments): Categorization of Testing Environments*)**: Advises that high-risk testing, fuzzing, or red-teaming should be performed on isolated staging, HIL test rigs, digital twins, or during scheduled downtime windows, rather than on live systems.  
* **Process-Informed Rate Limiting (*[Implementation 2.1.1](#implementation-2.1.1:-implement-baseline-rate-limiting):* Implement Baseline Rate Limiting)**: Clarified that rate limits should be dynamic and process-informed ([Implementation 2.1.2: Develop Process-Informed Guardrails](#implementation-2.1.2:-develop-process-informed-guardrails)) rather than fixed ceilings, so that valid high-volume commands are less likely to be suppressed during abnormal process upsets.  
* **Time-to-Divergence Cadence (*[Implementation 2.3.4](#implementation-2.3.4:-recurrent-risk-evaluations): Recurrent Risk Evaluations*)**: Introduced quantitative *Time-to-Divergence* baselining during staging to dictate model risk evaluation schedules as a fraction of estimated drift velocity.  
* **Consequence-Driven Risk Thresholds (*[Implementation 3.1.3](#implementation-3.1.3:-define-acceptable-risk-thresholds-and-associated-control-responses):* Define Acceptable Risk Thresholds and Associated Control Responses)**: Warns against over-indexing on CVSS or raw confidence scores, directing organizations to consequence-driven frameworks like SSVC.  
* **Non-Human Identity (NHI) Enforcement (*[Implementation 5.1.1](#implementation-5.1.1:-audit-for-and-replace-shared-credentials,-service-accounts,-secrets,-passwords,-and-api-keys):* Audit for and Replace Shared Credentials, Service Accounts, Secrets, Passwords, and API Keys)**: Specifies distinct cryptographic identities per sub-agent/tool invocation and warns against sharing enterprise API keys or master service accounts across agent nodes.  
* **Compensating Controls for Silent Updates (*[Implementation 6.1.1](#implementation-6.1.1:-add-si-disclosure-to-existing-procurement-policies): Add SI Disclosure to Existing Procurement Policies* *& [Implementation 6.1.2](#implementation-6.1.2:-require-sibom-for-mission-critical-applications):* Require SIBOM for Mission-Critical Applications)**: Added alternative controls (perimeter staging, egress gates, safety wrapper tightening) when suspending automated vendor updates is unfeasible, and reframed AIBOM compliance as a flexible gradient.  
* **Logical Policy Locks (*[Implementation 7.3.3](#implementation-7.3.3:-freeze-adaptation-of-online-learning-si-systems-during-operational-windows):* Freeze Adaptation of Online-Learning SI Systems During Operational Windows)**: Specifies automated “Policy Locks” to programmatically freeze model weights, hyperparameters, and boundary logic for adaptive/online-learning models during operational windows.  
* **Substrate Substitution Triage (*[Implementation 7.5.4](#implementation-7.5.4:-audit-interoperability-for-hardware-or-data-substrate-substitution): Audit Interoperability for Hardware or Data Substrate Substitution*)**: Expanded component replacement change-management logic into a 3-tier triage approach (unrelated vs. non-critical vs. safety-critical paths requiring full regression).  
* **Forensic Interpretability Gap (*[Implementation 8.1.2](#implementation-8.1.2:-identify-si-systems-that-may-not-satisfy-root-cause-analysis-requirements):* Identify SI Systems that May Not Satisfy Root Cause Analysis Requirements)**: Added new citations and warnings emphasizing that post-hoc explanations (SHAP/LIME) are ungrounded “reconstructed narratives” and should not satisfy forensic requirements.

### 4\. New Appendices {#4\.-new-appendices}

* **[Appendix B](#appendix-b:-scenario-to-practice-mapping)** **(*Scenario-to-Practice Mapping*)**: Added a complete table mapping 32 real-world incidents (i1–i32) across CI sectors directly to the 12 Practices to justify governance controls.  
* **[Appendix A](#appendix-a:-trustworthiness-characteristics)** **& C**: Designated explicit placeholders for *Trustworthiness Characteristics* (App A) and *Use Cases & Operational Scenarios* (App C).

  ## **Jul 7, 2026**

[^1]:  On Sept. 29, 2026, Executive Order 14434 directed U.S. executive branch agencies, including NIST, to refer to “Super Intelligence” (SI) rather than “Artificial Intelligence” (AI). In this document, “SI” refers to the same systems defined as Artificial Intelligence in 15 U.S.C. § 9401\. The term “AI” may still appear in cited works, proper names, quotations, established terms of art, and keyword lists.

[^2]:  This is the current working title and may change between now and final publication.

[^3]:  The NIST AI Risk Management Framework version 1.0, published in 2023, is the current version and referenced as a prior publication. This will be updated when the next version is released.

[^4]:  Former NIST employee; all work for this publication was done while at NIST.
